title: Topology document
description: topology.yaml — where an environment's hosted components actually run: regions, zones, replica ranges and one sentence of scaling intent. A description for a reviewer, not an infrastructure manifest, and never a second membership channel. Specified in framework/spec/kinds/environment.md; no portal code parses it.

$schema.description: The dialect discriminator (0015-artifact-dialects); the canonical value is this schema's own $id. Deliberately unpinned rather than const: a value naming some other dialect is W_ARTIFACT_DIALECT, a warning, read as the legacy dialect and never broken — a const here would restate that ruling as a hard rejection in the one place a severity cannot be relaxed. The loader strips the key once it has recorded the dialect, so nothing downstream ever sees it — including on the day something finally parses this file.

regions.description: The regions this environment occupies. Absent means a single unnamed region — not an unknown one.

hosts.description: Placement detail, one entry per hosted component or subtree. It ANNOTATES members and never creates them: membership is authored on the component side as a uses edge to this environment, and an entry for a component that does not declare it is W_ENV_HOST_UNDECLARED — a warning, because during a rollout the topology may legitimately lead the component's own declaration by a commit or two.

^x-.description: The escape hatch reaches into this artifact, at the top level and inside entries. Tolerated and ignored by the portal; any other unknown key is E_ENV_TOPOLOGY_SCHEMA. No top-level version: both environment siblings are part of the entity's version snapshot and carry no version field of their own.

name.description: Unique within the file — a fact about the list, and therefore not statable here: uniqueItems compares whole entries, not one member of each. Free-form beyond the casing (eu-west-1, store-berlin).

zones.description: Failure domains inside the region ([a, b, c]). An empty list and an absent one are indistinguishable to this schema, though they are not the same claim — one catalog file says so in its own notes.

notes.description: Prose; may be multi-line. The only field here with no length bound.

component.description: MUST resolve to a component or a product (E_ENV_TARGET_KIND). A product target is shorthand for every component beneath it, with these settings; the most specific entry wins, so a subtree entry plus an explicit entry for one descendant is an override rather than a conflict.

regions.description: Each name MUST be declared in the document's own regions list (E_ENV_REGION_UNKNOWN) — a cross-reference inside one document, which stock 2020-12 cannot make. Absent means placement is NOT RECORDED, and specifically not "everywhere".

scaling.description: One human sentence: the trigger, not the YAML of an autoscaler.

replicas.description: A fixed count is { min: n, max: n } — the format has one way to write a number and it is a range with equal ends. min MUST be <= max (E_ENV_TOPOLOGY_SCHEMA), which is the one clause of ENV4 no stock 2020-12 document can state: comparing two sibling properties is outside the vocabulary.

srn-ref.description: An ordinary SRN reference. Relative forms resolve against the artifact's own URI, srn://{solution}/environment/{name}/topology.yaml, so the solution-absolute form is strongly preferred — it is shorter and it survives the environment being renamed. An artifact suffix is refused (ENV11): hosts name entities, and an artifact has no kind.
